summary: Technical discovery to understand Prism Labs' p95 latency and throughput goals and decide whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private deployment fits their constraints. Customer needs: sub-200ms p95 for short-chat paths, 300-500ms p95 for longer streaming outputs, ability to sustain 1.2k concurrent chat sessions during peaks with graceful degradation. Action: Redwood to run tailored throughput tests and share cost tradeoffs.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-21
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM); Aisha (CTO Prism), Diego (DevOps), Tariq (ML Eng), Maya (Product)

[00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:10] Aisha (Prism CTO): hi all, Aisha here — I'll kick us off. we run Prism's conversational assistant and are evaluating infra for low-latency multi-tenant traffic.
[00:22] Samira: great, today Marcus will dig into throughput and p95 behaviors and we'll surface hosted versus dedicated versus private tradeoffs.
[00:30] Marcus (Redwood SE): yep. quick ask — can you confirm your p95 goals and typical input lengths?
[00:36] Maya (Product): our short Q&A path target is 150-200ms p95, that's 16 tokens average input + 32 tokens output. for long form summaries we're okay with 300-500ms p95 as long as streaming feels smooth.
[00:49] Tariq (ML Eng): and during marketing pushes we see spikes — last campaign hit about ~1.2k concurrent chat sessions sustained for 12 minutes, each generating ~60 tokens on average.
[00:59] Diego (DevOps): and we need no customer data leaving our VPC for some of the regulated teams — so private deployment is possible for a subset.
[01:10] Marcus: ok good. couple of clarifying Qs: are you using streaming on the client side (progressive tokens) or do you buffer and return whole responses?
[01:20] Maya: streaming. we show partials to users, so tail latency and token-per-second matter.
[01:26] Marcus: noted, that'll change how we think about batching and KV cache. Redwood's streaming path can keep tail latency low while sustaining higher token/sec, but you trade some throughput efficiency.
[01:40] Aisha: and what's the difference in behavior between hosted and dedicated here? e.g., do we lose caching benefits on hosted or is it comparable?
[01:50] Marcus: good question. hosted gives you shared model runners but we do prefix/KV caching per-tenant when pinned; it depends on whether you pin a model or let routing be flexible. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools so quieter variance and no noisy neighbor risk — better for tight p95 SLAs. private gives you the same runtime but customer-managed networking and KMS.
[02:10] Diego: security — if we go hosted, can we get VPC peering or private link? and KMS for key material?
[02:18] Samira: yes, Hosted supports private connectivity via PrivateLink in our regions and we integrate with customer KMS for encryption at rest. we'll share the SOC2 docs.
[02:28] Aisha: sounds good. Marcus, show us numbers — what's realistic for our token/sec and p95 with a 7B and a 13B model?
[02:36] Marcus: sure. rough ballpark from similar customers: 7B in hosted mode — for a streaming path with small tokens (16 in, 32 out) you can see p95s around 120-220ms depending on concurrency and batching. throughput-wise for continuous streaming that maps to ~70-200 tokens/sec per GPU core depending on sequence length and batching profile. 13B pushes latencies up — p95 for same traffic closer to 200-350ms unless you run dedicated optimized kernels or quantized variants.
[03:10] Tariq: when you say "per GPU core" what instance types are we talking about? A100? H100?
[03:16] Marcus: most of these numbers are A100 80GB equiv in our hosted fleet; H100 will improve p95 by 10-25% for medium-long sequences. also quantization (int8/4) changes throughput a lot but you need to accept some possible quality delta.
[03:32] Diego: our regulated tenants will require private deployment on-prem for now. can Redwood runtime be deployed air-gapped?
[03:38] Marcus: yes, we have a private deployment package for air-gapped infra. it includes the runtime, model artifacts, and orchestration — you'll manage KMS and the control plane is customer-hosted. note: feature parity for some observability modules is slightly different (we ship logs and metrics but retention policies are customer-managed).
[03:58] Maya: on concurrency — that 1.2k concurrent sessions, is that chats open or active token-generating?
[04:03] Tariq: overlap — about 60% were actively generating tokens during the peak, others were idling with open sockets. so peak active concurrency ~720.
[04:12] Marcus: ok that matters. if active concurrency ~720 and each active session is 60 tokens output at say 40 tokens/sec streaming, you need backend token/sec capacity ~28.8k tokens/sec sustained during the 12-minute window. translating to GPUs — depends on model and batching, but rough estimate for 7B dedicated optimized config might be 4-6 GPUs for steady state with margin; hosted might require autoscale with burst allowance.
[04:40] Diego: that's useful. can you run a token-rate benchmark using our sample prompt set to validate this?
[04:45] Samira: yes, Marcus can run a tailored benchmark. Marcus, what do you need from Prism?
[04:50] Marcus: a sample of prompts (2-3K) representing distribution, target concurrency shapes (ramp up profile), and a golden p95 target per path. also confirm if we should test in hosted sandbox or mimic private config (quant rigs).
[05:05] Aisha: we'll share prompts and a traffic trace. our golden p95 for short path is 180ms and for streaming long path we want 400ms p95 max.
[05:15] Marcus: perfect. we'll run suite with 7B/13B and with and without prefix/K-V cache to show delta. note: KV cache was transcribed here earlier in other calls as K-V cash in our logs, so apologies for the occasional transcript typos.
[05:30] Priya (CSM): on reuse and caching — do you rely on session affinity? because affinity changes cache hit rate and impacts p95.
[05:39] Tariq: we have sticky sessions for some customers, but for scale we prefer stateless. can Redwood offer replicating prefix caches across nodes?
[05:47] Marcus: we do prefix caching at request router level and can replicate hot entries to reduce cold start. replication increases memory overhead but lowers p95 for repeated prompts. for stateless we rely more on micro-batching.
[05:58] Diego: micro-batching — doesn't that increase tail latency for streaming?
[06:03] Marcus: it can if you wait to fill batches. Redwood uses adaptive batching: for streaming we favor low-delay paths and break batches early if a request needs fast turn. you pay some throughput cost, but tail latency stays low.
[06:18] Aisha: any known noisy neighbor incidents on hosted that bumped p95? we worry about shared tenancy during campaign spikes.
[06:26] Marcus: historically rare — our scheduler isolates high token/sec flows and can pin customers to dedicated lanes short-term. for strict SLAs we recommend dedicated pools. hosted has SLAs but actual p95 can vary during extreme global spikes.
[06:40] Maya: pricing tradeoffs — can you outline high-level delta between hosted and dedicated for our projected peak?
[06:46] Samira: high-level: Hosted = low setup, usage billing per token and per-embedding; Dedicated = monthly reserved GPU cost plus lower unit token cost and guaranteed pool. we will send a modelled worksheet with your traffic profile. it shows break-even typically at sustained 30-40% utilization of dedicated pool versus pulsing hosted.
[07:10] Tariq: any limitations around model variants — for example can we bring our own fine-tuned models into hosted?
[07:16] Marcus: yes, BYOM is supported for Dedicated and Private; hosted supports custom models with additional review — private is the easiest for fully proprietary fine-tunes.
[07:25] Diego: what about telemetry and observability — per-token tracing and cost attribution?
[07:31] Priya: our console gives token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and tracing hooks. in Private you'll ship logs to your cluster or we can integrate with forwarders.
[07:41] Aisha: let's talk failure modes — if a GPU node fails during a burst, what's the graceful fallback?
[07:47] Marcus: we do smart routing: fallback to a smaller model on the same pool or route to another region/dedicated fallback. we can set policies: strict throughput fallback or best-effort latency fallback. you'll decide per-route.
[07:59] Maya: how about quantization? you mentioned int4 earlier — is quality hit measurable?
[08:04] Marcus: depends on model and prompts. for many instruction-following tasks int8/4 can be indistinguishable for business metrics but for specialized generation we run evals. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles per workload.
[08:16] Tariq: do you have standard benchmark artifacts we can review?
[08:20] Samira: yes we'll share recent token/sec and p95 benchmark spreadsheets and a sample run report showing methodology.
[08:26] Diego: let's set an expectation for the test: we need numbers that separate steady-state from burst. can Redwood provide both sustained throughput and 1-10 minute burst profiles?
[08:36] Marcus: absolutely. we'll do sustained 30-minute run and a 12-minute burst to mirror your campaign. we'll include cold-start and warm cache scenarios.
[08:45] Aisha: on security checklist items: SSO (SAML), audit logs, retention controls, and data residency — can you confirm?
[08:53] Samira: yes: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and region-specific hosting options. for Private we'll co-manage retention policies. we'll attach SOC2 and ISO snippets.
[09:05] Maya: who will own the pilot? timeline wise we want to run a 2-week pilot starting ~2026-10-26 if possible.
[09:14] Samira: that seems doable; we often run 2-week pilots. Marcus, can you commit to delivering benchmark by 10/28?
[09:20] Marcus: yes, I'll run an initial sweep by 10/28 and share raw artifacts.
[09:24] Diego: and Samira you'll send contract/pricing?
[09:27] Samira: yes. I'll send a draft and cost worksheet by 10/23.
[09:31] Tariq: small nit — do you allow hooking our internal KMS for hosted via customer-managed keys?
[09:36] Marcus: we support customer KMS integration for both hosted (with PrivateLink) and Private. some key attestation steps are required. we'll include a checklist.
[09:45] Maya: okay, sounds like clear next steps.
[09:49] Samira: recap: Prism to send prompts and traffic shape (Diego/Aisha), Redwood to run benchmark (Marcus) and share pricing + security docs (Samira), schedule security deep-dive next week (Priya to co-ordinate).
[10:03] Aisha: thanks, appreciate the detailed answers.
[10:07] Samira: thanks everyone. ending now.

[10:15] End of recording.
